name: Samuel
overview: Samuel was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, uniquely identified as the son of Tola according to 1 Chronicles 7:2. The biblical record does not provide additional personal details beyond this lineage. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation and paternal descent.
namesAndTitles: The name Samuel means 'his name is God' or 'heard of God,' reflecting a connection to the divine name El, as noted in 1 Chronicles 7:2. This proper name highlights a recognition of God's presence and activity in his life.
familyAndRelationships: Samuel is explicitly recorded as the son of Tola, establishing his family connection within the tribe of Issachar. No other familial relationships are documented in the given scriptural reference.
scriptureSignificance: Samuel holds a pivotal role in the biblical narrative as the last judge and a prophet who anointed Israel's first kings, Saul and David. His life marks the critical transition from the period of judges to the establishment of the monarchy, demonstrating faithful obedience to God's direction. His dedication to God's service from childhood and his leadership in Israel underscore his importance in God's unfolding plan.
